questions.stem: Suppose you are going to write a proposal to your student union for enriching students’ extracurricular activities. You are to write about what activities to organize and why. You will have 30 minutes to write the proposal. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
A Proposal on Enriching Extracurricular Activities

I am writing to propose a few extracurricular activities that our student union could organize, in the hope of making our campus life more colorful and rewarding.

To begin with, I would suggest holding a monthly book-sharing club. Since many of us read alone and seldom exchange thoughts, such a club would offer a regular chance to share insights, broaden our horizons and improve our critical thinking.

In addition, I recommend arranging weekend volunteer trips to nearby communities. These activities would not only allow us to apply what we learn in real life, but also cultivate a stronger sense of social responsibility and teamwork among students.

I sincerely hope the student union will take these suggestions into consideration. Your support would mean a great deal to all of us. Thank you for your time and attention.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 本场次听力只有一份音频，本套听力与同场第一套同卷；原文、题目与答案取自该套真题。考场多套卷的选项顺序可能不同，这里沿用第一套的顺序。在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: A new study finds that beverages containing added sugar might be harmful.
transcript.zh: 一项新研究发现，含添加糖的饮料可能有害健康。

transcript.text: In the study, researchers analyzed information from over 80,000 women and 37,000 men. Participants worked in the health profession. They were followed for approximately three decades. They completed surveys about their diet every four years. They also answered questions about sleep and exercise and health every two years.
transcript.zh: 在该研究中，研究人员分析了超过8万名女性和3.7万名男性的信息。参与者从事健康专业工作。他们被跟踪随访了约三十年。他们每四年完成一次关于饮食的调查。他们还每两年回答关于睡眠、运动和健康的问题。

transcript.text: The more beverages containing added sugar that people drank, the greater their risk of death was during the study period.
transcript.zh: 人们饮用的含添加糖饮料越多，他们在研究期间的死亡风险就越大。

transcript.text: These beverages included soda, energy drinks and sports drinks. Beverages like pure fruit juice which are sweet but do not contain added sugar were not part of the study.
transcript.zh: 这些饮料包括苏打水、能量饮料和运动饮料。像纯果汁这样味甜但不含添加糖的饮料不在本研究范围内。

transcript.text: The findings held even after the researchers considered other factors that could affect people's health. These factors included lack of exercise and not eating enough vegetables. They also included consuming too much meat.
transcript.zh: 即使在研究人员考虑了其他可能影响人们健康的因素后，这些发现仍然成立。这些因素包括缺乏运动和蔬菜摄入不足。它们还包括肉类摄入过多。

transcript.text: The scientists say that their results support limiting beverages with added sugar. They argue we should replace them with other drinks, with water being the best choice. However, the researchers admit this is simply their recommendation. The study found only an association: It did not prove that drinks with added sugar cause early death.
transcript.zh: 科学家们表示，他们的研究结果支持限制含添加糖的饮料。他们主张我们应该用其他饮料代替它们，其中水是最佳选择。然而，研究人员承认这只是他们的建议。该研究仅发现了一种关联：它并未证明含添加糖的饮料会导致过早死亡。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the new study from the news report?

options.text: It studied the effects of exercise on sleep.
Its participants came from various walks of life.
Its findings confirmed those of previous studies.
It ran for as long as some thirty years.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：They were followed for approximately three decades.信号：时长事实 three decades 。答案句的信号是一个明确的时长数据 followed for approximately three decades，three decades 即三十年；新闻里凡出现具体年限、…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 说研究的是运动对睡眠的影响，盗用了录音 questions about sleep and exercise 里真出现过的 sleep、exercise 两个原词；但录音里这两项只是参与者被问到的调查内容之一，本研究的真正主题是含糖饮料与死亡风险，并非研究运动对睡眠的影响，听到原词就选正中圈套。 借用原文：Participants worked in the health profession.
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：B 说参与者来自各行各业（various walks of life），但录音明说 Participants worked in the health profession.，即都是医疗卫生行业的人；B 与原文事实相反，是对参与者构成的曲解。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C 说本研究证实了以往研究的结论，但录音通篇没提与任何 previous studies 的比较，反而在结尾强调 it did not prove that drinks with added sugar cause early death——只是关联、未下定论；C 属录音根本没说的内容。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（approximately three decades ↔ as long as some thirty years three decades = thirty years）

questions.evidenceText: They were followed for approximately three decades.

questions.stem: What is the scientists' recommendation?

options.text: Eating more vegetables instead of meats.
Drinking water instead of beverages with added sugar.
Consuming more energy drinks and sports drinks.
Forming the habit of exercising regularly.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：They argue we should replace them with other drinks, with water being the best choice.信号：建议句 should + 最佳选择 。答案句同时出现两个强信号：建议词 we should replace them 和择优表达 water being the best choice；should 表建议、the …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 说多吃蔬菜代替肉，盗用了录音 not eating enough vegetables 与 consuming too much meat 里出现过的 vegetables、meat；但录音里这两项是研究者考虑过的其他影响健康的因素，不是科学家给出的建议，把干扰因素当成建议正是陷阱。 借用原文：These beverages included soda, energy drinks and sports drinks.
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 让人多喝能量饮料和运动饮料，盗用录音 soda, energy drinks and sports drinks 里的原词；但录音明确说这些正是含糖饮料、应当限制，C 把该少喝的说成多喝，与原文意思相反。 借用原文：These factors included lack of exercise
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说养成规律运动的习惯，盗用录音 lack of exercise 里的 exercise；但运动同样只是研究者排查的其他健康因素之一，录音从未把规律运动作为科学家的建议提出，D 答非所问。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（replace them with other drinks, with water being the best choice ↔ Drinking water instead of beverages with added sugar 用水替换＝喝水代替）

questions.evidenceText: They argue we should replace them with other drinks, with water being the best choice.

transcript.text: German police appealed Friday for information about the possible owners of two 17th-century oil paintings.
transcript.zh: 德国警方周五呼吁民众提供有关两幅17世纪油画可能所有者的信息。

transcript.text: Police said a 64-year-old man found the paintings in a garbage pile at a highway rest stop last month. He later handed them in to the Cologne police.
transcript.zh: 警方表示,一名64岁男子上个月在高速公路休息站的垃圾堆中发现了这些画作。他后来将它们交给了科隆警方。

transcript.text: An initial assessment by an art expert concluded the two framed paintings were originals, police said.
transcript.zh: 警方称,一位艺术专家的初步评估认定这两幅带框画作是原作。

transcript.text: One is a landscape painted by the Italian artist Pietro Bellotti dating to 1665. The other is a painting of a boy by the 17th-century Dutch artist Samuel van Hoogstraten, date unknown. Their combined worth is estimated to be around one million euros.
transcript.zh: 其中一幅是意大利艺术家Pietro Bellotti于1665年创作的风景画。另一幅是17世纪荷兰艺术家Samuel van Hoogstraten创作的男孩肖像画,创作日期不详。两幅画的总价值估计约为一百万欧元。

transcript.text: Authorities have not yet confirmed what will happen if the rightful owner is not found. Nevertheless, it is speculated that they could either be handed over to the National Art Museum of Cologne or sold to the public by the local government.
transcript.zh: 当局尚未确认如果找不到合法所有者将如何处理。不过,有人推测这些画作可能会被移交给科隆国家美术馆,或由地方政府向公众出售。

questions.stem: What did German police say about a 64-year-old man?

options.text: He asked them about his lost paintings.
He knew the owner of two missing paintings.
He left his paintings at a highway rest stop.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Police said a 64-year-old man found the paintings in a garbage pile at a highway rest stop last month.信号：对象出场即答案句 。录音念到 a 64-year-old man 这个题干点名的对象时，紧跟其后的动词 found the paintings 就是答案落点——细节题的答案句信号，就是题干那个专有对象一出现。

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：选项把 his lost paintings 安在男子头上，可录音说的是他在垃圾堆里发现（found）画并上交，画不是他丢的、更不是他来打听自己丢的画，方向正好反了。
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项盗用了录音 owners、rightful owner 里反复出现的 owner 一词，编出 "他认识两幅失踪画的主人"，可录音只说警方在找失主，从没说这位男子认识失主，是听到 owner 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：at a highway rest stop
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项盗用录音 at a highway rest stop 这个真地点，却把动作篡改成 left（把画留在那里），而录音说的是他在那里 found（发现）画，地点是真的、动作是假的，典型原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（found the paintings ↔ found two 17th-century oil paintings the paintings 还原为完整名称）

questions.evidenceText: Police said a 64-year-old man found the paintings in a garbage pile at a highway rest stop last month.

questions.stem: What is the art expert's conclusion about the two framed paintings?

options.text: They were stolen by an Italian boy.
They came from the same artist.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：An initial assessment by an art expert concluded the two framed paintings were originals, police said.信号：结论动词 concluded 引出定性 。录音里 An initial assessment by an art expert concluded 用 concluded（得出结论）这个下结论的信号词，后面紧跟的 w…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：选项 imitations（赝品）与专家结论 were originals（真迹）意思正好相反，是把定性极性反转的陷阱；A、B 一真一假对立，听准 originals 就该排除 A。 借用原文：a painting of a boy by the 17th-century Dutch artist
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项盗用录音第 4 段 the Italian artist 的 Italian 和 a painting of a boy 的 boy，拼成 "被一个意大利男孩偷走"，可录音根本没提偷画，画里有个男孩、画家是意大利人都被偷换成了偷窃情节，原词陷阱。 借用原文：One is a landscape painted by the Italian artist Pietro Bellotti dating to 1665. The other is a painting of a boy by the 17th-century Dutch artist Samuel van Hoogstraten
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：录音第 4 段明说一幅是意大利画家 Pietro Bellotti 所作、另一幅出自荷兰画家 Samuel van Hoogstraten，是两位不同画家；选项却说出自 same artist，与原文事实直接矛盾。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（were originals ↔ They are originals. 几乎原句保留）

questions.evidenceText: An initial assessment by an art expert concluded the two framed paintings were originals, police said.

transcript.text: A four-year-old girl has walked eight kilometers through a snowy forest to seek help for her sick grandmother who later died of a heart attack. The young girl braved the threat of bears, wolves and temperatures far below freezing. She made the journey through a remote region in Siberia after waking up to find her grandmother motionless.
transcript.zh: 一名四岁女孩在雪地森林中步行八公里为生病的祖母寻求帮助，祖母后来死于心脏病发作。这名年幼的女孩冒着熊、狼和远低于冰点的气温威胁，在醒来发现祖母一动不动后，穿越西伯利亚偏远地区完成了这段旅程。

transcript.text: Named locally as Karla, she lives alone with her elderly grandmother and her blind grandfather. As a result, the girl's mother is facing a criminal case. She stands accused of leaving a minor in danger in the care of the elderly. She also faces investigation from childcare services, who will also be asking why Karla was left alone with her vulnerable relatives.
transcript.zh: 当地称她为Karla，她独自与年迈的祖母和失明的祖父生活在一起。因此，女孩的母亲面临刑事诉讼。她被指控将未成年人置于危险之中，交由老年人照顾。她还面临儿童保育服务部门的调查，该部门也将询问为何让Karla独自与她脆弱的亲属待在一起。

transcript.text: The journey took place in February when temperatures average negative 26 degrees Celsius. Russian reports on social media suggest the forest may have been as cold as negative 34 degrees Celsius. The journey was only recently confirmed by authorities.
transcript.zh: 这段旅程发生在二月，当时平均气温为零下26摄氏度。俄罗斯社交媒体报道称，森林中的温度可能低至零下34摄氏度。这段旅程直到最近才得到当局确认。

transcript.text: But though she was suffering from the effects of extreme cold, the child reportedly suffered no life-threatening effects. Last year, a three-year-old boy survived alone for three days in a remote forest in the same region.
transcript.zh: 尽管她遭受了极寒的影响,但据报道这名儿童没有出现危及生命的症状。去年，一名三岁男孩在同一地区的偏远森林中独自生存了三天。

questions.stem: What did the four-year-old girl attempt to do?

options.text: Flee from the threat of bears.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A four-year-old girl has walked eight kilometers through a snowy forest to seek help for her sick grandmother who later died of a heart attack.信号：目的状语 to seek help for 直指意图 。本句用不定式目的状语 to seek help for her sick grandmother 点明女孩此行的目的——"问意图"的题，答案就藏在 to do …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音第 2 段确实念到 her blind grandfather，A 项 Look after her grandfather. 就盗用这个"爷爷"原词制造"听到就选"的诱惑；但女孩求助的对象是奶奶不是爷爷，对象张冠李戴。 借用原文：through a remote region in Siberia
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音念到 through a remote region in Siberia，B 项 Leave the remote cold region. 盗用 remote region 把女孩动机歪曲成"为自己离开寒冷地区"；实际她是为奶奶求助而穿越该地区，不是想离开它。 借用原文：braved the threat of bears
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音念到 braved the threat of bears，D 项 Flee from the threat of bears. 把这个醒目画面词搬进选项；但原文是说女孩"冒着"熊的威胁去求助，不是"为逃避熊"才出门，目的被偷换。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（to seek help for her sick grandmother ↔ Save her sick grandmother. 为奶奶求助=救奶奶（概括同义））

questions.evidenceText: A four-year-old girl has walked eight kilometers through a snowy forest to seek help for her sick grandmother who later died of a heart attack.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about the girl's mother?

options.text: She has to face a criminal charge.
She was found lying motionless in the snow.
She searched for her daughter in freezing cold.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：As a result, the girl's mother is facing a criminal case. She stands accused of leaving a minor in danger in the care of the elderly.信号：专门讲 mother 的那句直接应答题干 。录音里唯一正面交代母亲的句子是 the girl's mother is facing a criminal case，紧接着用 stands accused of 补充指…

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：录音第 1 段说"奶奶"被发现时 motionless，B 项 She was found lying motionless in the snow. 把这个画面安到"母亲"头上；motionless 是原词，但躺着不动的是奶奶不是妈妈。 借用原文：She also faces investigation from childcare services
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：录音通篇讲严寒（negative 26 degrees Celsius 等），C 项 She searched for her daughter in freezing cold. 借"严寒"主题编出"母亲冒寒找女儿"的情节；但原文从没说母亲外出寻找，是女孩自己出门求助。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音念到 investigation from childcare services，D 项 She works in childcare services. 盗用 childcare services 这个机构词；但原文是该机构要"调查"这件事，不是说母亲"在那儿工作"。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（is facing a criminal case ↔ She has to face a criminal charge. 面临刑事案件=要面临刑事指控（近义词替换））

questions.evidenceText: As a result, the girl's mother is facing a criminal case. She stands accused of leaving a minor in danger in the care of the elderly.

questions.stem: What happened to the little girl according to the news report?

options.text: She was found in a forest after three days.
She lay totally unconscious for three days.
She suffered from the effects of severe cold.
She was finally rescued by her relatives.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：But though she was suffering from the effects of extreme cold, the child reportedly suffered no life-threatening effects.信号：末段交代结果，让步状语 though 引出真实状况 。答案落在末段交代女孩结局的一句，信号是让步连词 though：though 引出的 suffering from the effects of extreme c…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：录音末句说"去年一个三岁男孩" survived alone for three days in a remote forest，A 项 She was found in a forest after three days. 盗用 forest 和 three days，把男孩的旧事安到这个女孩头上。 借用原文：the child reportedly suffered no life-threatening effects
optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：B 项 She lay totally unconscious for three days. 借男孩那句的 three days 拼出"女孩昏迷三天"；原文既没说女孩昏迷，也没说她经历三天，no life-threatening effects 反而说明她无大碍，程度被严重夸大。 借用原文：to seek help for her sick grandmother
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：录音里女孩是"独自外出为亲属求助"，D 项 She was finally rescued by her relatives. 把方向反过来说成"被亲属救出"；relatives 算原文涉及的关系词，但谁救谁正相反。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（suffering from the effects of extreme cold ↔ She suffered from the effects of severe cold. extreme cold=severe cold（近义形容词替换））

questions.evidenceText: But though she was suffering from the effects of extreme cold, the child reportedly suffered no life-threatening effects.

transcript.text: W: I've made a new friend recently. Her name is Susan and she's from South Africa.
transcript.zh: W: 我最近交了个新朋友。她叫Susan，来自南非。

transcript.text: M: How did you meet her?
transcript.zh: M: 你们怎么认识的？

transcript.text: W: We met over WeChat. She has very cool photos on her social media. The photos of her hometown look amazing.
transcript.zh: W: 我们在微信上认识的。她社交媒体上的照片很酷。她家乡的照片看起来棒极了。

transcript.text: M: What's her hometown called?
transcript.zh: M: 她家乡叫什么？

transcript.text: W: It's called Cape Town. It's in the southwest of South Africa. She says it's very green and windy. The city was built by European settlers. And there's a big mountain that overlooks the city. The mountain is called Table Mountain because it's flat at the top.
transcript.zh: W: 叫开普敦。在南非西南部。她说那里很绿，风很大。这座城市是欧洲殖民者建的。还有一座大山俯瞰着这座城市。这座山叫桌山，因为它顶部是平的。

transcript.text: M: That sounds interesting. What are the people there like?
transcript.zh: M: 听起来很有意思。那里的人怎么样？

transcript.text: W: Well, Susan says South Africa is very mixed. There are black people and white people and Indian people. Susan is white. She says her ancestors were from Britain. Many languages are spoken in South Africa, but she only speaks English.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，Susan说南非种族很多元。有黑人、白人和印度人。Susan是白人。她说她的祖先来自英国。南非说很多种语言，但她只说英语。

transcript.text: M: Didn't South Africa host the Football World Cup a few years ago? They must play football a lot then, right?
transcript.zh: M: 南非不是几年前举办过足球世界杯吗？那他们一定很常踢足球吧？

transcript.text: W: I think they play football, but it's not as popular as rugby.
transcript.zh: W: 我想他们踢足球，但没有橄榄球那么流行。

transcript.text: M: Rugby? What's rugby?
transcript.zh: M: 橄榄球？橄榄球是什么？

transcript.text: W: Rugby is a sport with two teams and the players carry the ball in their arms and throw it at each other. The ball is not round and the players push each other. I don't really understand the rules. I think it's very complicated.
transcript.zh: W: 橄榄球是一项两队对抗的运动，球员用手臂抱着球互相传递。球不是圆的，球员之间会互相推搡。我不太懂规则。我觉得挺复杂的。

transcript.text: M: That sounds like a very strange sport indeed. Is it only South Africa that plays it?
transcript.zh: M: 听起来确实是项很奇怪的运动。只有南非玩这个吗？

transcript.text: W: No, it's also popular in Britain and in other former British colonies like Australia and New Zealand.
transcript.zh: W: 不是，在英国和其他前英国殖民地像澳大利亚、新西兰也很流行。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her new friend Susan?

options.text: She shows a real passion for taking photos.
She has just returned from her hometown.
She comes from the city of Cape Town.
She has a truly amazing appearance.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Her name is Susan and she's from South Africa.信号：女士介绍朋友的开场陈述 。对话一开口，女士就主动交代 she's from South Africa，这是"被介绍人的出身"，正面回答了"关于 Susan"。随后第5段又点出家乡 It's called Cape T…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音说的是 She has very cool photos on her social media.——朋友圈有好照片，并没说她"热爱拍照"。选项把"有酷照片"偷换成"对拍照有热情"，是听到 photos 就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：The photos of her hometown look amazing.
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音里 hometown 出现在 The photos of her hometown look amazing.，说的是"家乡的照片好看"，根本没说她"刚从家乡回来"。选项借 hometown 这个原词编了个时间动作。 借用原文：The photos of her hometown look amazing.
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：录音里 amazing 形容的是 The photos of her hometown look amazing.——家乡的照片惊艳，不是说"她本人长相惊艳"。选项把形容"照片"的词安到了"她的外貌"上。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（she's from South Africa ↔ She comes from the city of Cape Town. from = comes from，国家细化到城市）

questions.evidenceText: Her name is Susan and she's from South Africa.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about Table Mountain?

options.text: It is as famous as Cape Town.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：The mountain is called Table Mountain because it's flat at the top.信号：因果 because 后给出命名缘由即特征 。The mountain is called Table Mountain because it's flat at the top. 中 because 后那句才是关键…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音提到 It's called Cape Town. 是城市名，但从没说桌山"和开普敦一样有名"。选项借 Cape Town 这个原词，凭空造了个"知名度比较"。 借用原文：it's very green and windy
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：录音说 it's very green and windy——这是形容开普敦这座城市"很绿、多风"，既不是说桌山，也没说"无污染"。选项把 green 扩大成 free from pollution，程度被悄悄拔高。 借用原文：The city was built by European settlers.
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：录音里 European settlers 出现在 The city was built by European settlers.——欧洲移民"建了这座城"，命名桌山的依据是"顶平"而非欧洲移民。选项把"建城"换成"给山命名"。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（it's flat at the top ↔ It has a flat surface at the top. flat at the top = flat surface at the top）

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：录音 South Africa is very mixed 说的是"南非（这个国家/人口）很混杂"，紧接着却明说 Susan is white.——她是白人，不是混血。选项把形容国家的 mixed 安到了她头上。 借用原文：Indian people

transcript.text: M: Hi, Jennifer. I'm really struggling with this semester's workload. Do you have any advice?
transcript.zh: M: 嗨，Jennifer。我这学期的课业负担真的让我很吃力。你有什么建议吗？

transcript.text: W: Have you considered making a study guide? It's a tool you can make yourself to take the stress out of studying. I've been using one since the start of last semester, and it has really helped relieve a lot of study pressure.
transcript.zh: W: 你考虑过做一个学习指南吗？这是一个你可以自己制作的工具，能减轻学习压力。从上学期开始我就一直在用，真的帮我缓解了很多学习压力。

transcript.text: M: Sounds like just what I need. My main problem is that my study folder is full of notes and worksheets, and is badly disorganized. I don't know where to start.
transcript.zh: M: 听起来正是我需要的。我的主要问题是我的学习文件夹里塞满了笔记和作业纸，而且乱七八糟的。我都不知道从哪儿开始。

transcript.text: W: Okay. Well, the main thing is to have everything in the right place. Whatever you're reviewing, it's important that it's arranged for your particular needs of that subject, and in the most user-friendly way you can. What kind of learner are you?
transcript.zh: W: 好的。嗯，最重要的是把所有东西都放对地方。不管你在复习什么，重要的是要按照你对那门科目的特定需求来安排，而且要用你能做到的最方便使用的方式。你是哪种类型的学习者？

transcript.text: M: Um, I'm not sure.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯，我不太确定。

transcript.text: W: Well, visual learners prefer using images, pictures, colors, and maps to organize information. Logical learners have a linear mind and would rather use logic, reasoning and systems. I'm an emotional learner, which means I need to connect to information emotionally to understand it.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，视觉型学习者更喜欢用图像、图片、颜色和地图来组织信息。逻辑型学习者有线性思维，更喜欢用逻辑、推理和系统。我是情感型学习者，这意味着我需要在情感上与信息建立联系才能理解它。

transcript.text: M: Oh! I'm very much dependent on vision as a way of taking in information.
transcript.zh: M: 哦！我非常依赖视觉作为接收信息的方式。

transcript.text: W: Well, I suggest reorganizing your notes using color-coded sections in your study guides, or using idea mapping to lay out the information and make it more quickly accessible.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，我建议你在学习指南里用颜色编码的分区来重新组织你的笔记，或者用思维导图来布局信息，让它更快速可查。

transcript.text: M: So you think I should arrange my notes using color and pictures in place of text.
transcript.zh: M: 所以你认为我应该用颜色和图片代替文字来安排我的笔记。

transcript.text: W: Yes, you'll probably start to grasp information a lot quicker that way. As an emotional learner, I organize my notes into a story that I can connect to and recite to myself.
transcript.zh: W: 对，这样你可能会更快地掌握信息。作为情感型学习者，我会把笔记组织成一个我能产生共鸣并能向自己复述的故事。

transcript.text: M: That's amazing. I didn't know there were so many different ways to learn.
transcript.zh: M: 太棒了。我都不知道原来有这么多不同的学习方式。

questions.stem: What does the woman advise the man to do?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Have you considered making a study guide? It's a tool you can make yourself to take the stress out of studying.信号：建议信号 Have you considered 引出的提议 。女方用 Have you considered making a study guide? 这个建议句式回应男方的求助，「考虑过……吗」就是典型的提建议…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：选项 Consult his advisors. 说的「咨询顾问」在整段对话里从未出现，女方建议的是自己做学习指南，不是去找顾问。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 Go over his notes regularly. 借了对话里反复出现的 notes 来诱你，但女方此处的建议是做 study guide，并未叫他「定期复习笔记」；regularly（定期）更是录音里没有的。 借用原文：take the stress out of studying
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 Take stress-relief sessions. 抓住录音里 take the stress out of studying 的 stress 做文章，但录音说的是「学习指南能卸掉压力」，不是叫他去「上减压课程」；stress-relief sessions 是凭 stress 一词编出来的。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Have you considered making a study guide? ↔ Prepare a study guide. making 改写成 Prepare，同义动词替换）

questions.stem: What is the biggest problem the man has with his studies?

options.text: He finds the workload too heavy.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：My main problem is that my study folder is full of notes and worksheets, and is badly disorganized.信号：强调信号 My main problem is 直接点题 。男方用 My main problem is 这个强调句式亲口点出最大困扰，main problem 就是直接指向答案的信号，其后描述的状况即为答案内容。

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：选项 His worksheets are terribly messy. 借了录音的 worksheets，但录音说乱的是整个 study folder，worksheets 只是文件夹里装着的东西之一；把「乱」单独安到 worksheets 头上是偷换对象。 借用原文：I'm really struggling with this semester's workload
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 He finds the workload too heavy. 抓住男方开场 struggling with this semester's workload 的 workload，但那只是他来求助的引子，他亲口说的 main problem 是文件夹乱，不是工作量大。 借用原文：my study folder is full of notes and worksheets
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 He has difficulty taking notes quickly. 借录音里的 notes 做文章，但录音只说文件夹里塞满 notes 且很乱，从没提男方「记笔记速度慢」这个困难，taking notes quickly 是凭 notes 一词编造的。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（my study folder is full of notes and worksheets, and is badly disorganized ↔ His study folder is badly disorganized. study folder 与 badly disorganized 原句几乎直取）

questions.stem: What kind of learner does the woman say she is?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：I'm an emotional learner, which means I need to connect to information emotionally to understand it.信号：第一人称自指 I'm an emotional learner 。女方在介绍完 visual、logical 两类后，用 I'm an emotional learner 这个第一人称自指句点明自己的类别，I'm 就…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：选项 A visual learner. 借了录音里 visual learners 这一类，但视觉型对应的是男方（他说 I'm very much dependent on vision），女方自称的是情感型；把男方的类别安给女方即张冠李戴。 借用原文：reorganizing your notes using color-coded sections
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 An organized learner. 蹭了全篇「整理笔记 organize」的氛围，但录音介绍的三类是 visual、logical、emotional，从没有 organized learner 这一类，更不是女方的自称。 借用原文：Logical learners have a linear mind and would rather use logic, reasoning and systems
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：选项 A logical learner. 取了录音 Logical learners have a linear mind 这一类，但那是女方泛指介绍的一类人，她自称的是 emotional，不是 logical；安到女方头上属张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I'm an emotional learner ↔ An emotional learner. emotional learner 原词对应）

options.text: Arrange them using color and pictures.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P8）：Well, I suggest reorganizing your notes using color-coded sections in your study guides, or using idea mapping to lay out the information.信号：建议信号 I suggest 引出给男方的方法 。女方用 I suggest reorganizing your notes using color-coded sections 直接给男方建议，I suggest …

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 Restructure them in a logical way. 借了录音介绍 logical learners 时的 logic 一词，但女方给男方（视觉型）的建议是用颜色和图，不是「按逻辑重构」；logical 属另一类学习者的特征。 借用原文：make it more quickly accessible

transcript.text: The golden rule is a moral principle which states that you should treat others the way you want to be treated yourself. For example, if you want people to treat you with respect, you should treat them with respect.
transcript.zh: 黄金法则是一条道德原则,它指出你应该以你希望被对待的方式对待他人。例如,如果你希望人们尊重你,你就应该尊重他们。

transcript.text: Different people tend to be exposed to different forms of the golden rule, based on factors such as the religion in their society.
transcript.zh: 不同的人往往会接触到不同形式的黄金法则,这取决于诸如其社会中的宗教等因素。

transcript.text: However, all forms of the golden rule revolve around the same concept. Namely, they help you treat others better, by using the way you yourself would want to be treated as a guide of how to behave.
transcript.zh: 然而,黄金法则的所有形式都围绕着同一个概念。也就是说,它们通过使用你自己希望被对待的方式作为行为指南,帮助你更好地对待他人。

transcript.text: A notable criticism of the golden rule is that its application can lead to undesirable outcomes, when it conflicts with laws and ethical principles.
transcript.zh: 对黄金法则的一个显著批评是,当它与法律和伦理原则相冲突时,其应用可能导致不良后果。

transcript.text: For example, if someone breaks the law, the golden rule would suggest that we should let them go, because we would not want to be punished ourselves.
transcript.zh: 例如,如果有人违法,黄金法则会建议我们应该放过他们,因为我们自己也不想受到惩罚。

transcript.text: However, this issue with the golden rule can be dealt with in a general manner, by viewing this principle as one of several principles that we use to guide our behavior as individuals and as a society.
transcript.zh: 然而,黄金法则的这一问题可以通过一般性方式来处理,即把这一原则视为我们用来指导个人和社会行为的若干原则之一。

transcript.text: Specifically, in the example described above, most individuals and societies choose to place laws and ethical principles above the golden rule. This means that they strive to implement the golden rule whenever possible, as long as it doesn't clash with a more important concept.
transcript.zh: 具体而言,在上述例子中,大多数个人和社会选择将法律和伦理原则置于黄金法则之上。这意味着只要不与更重要的概念发生冲突,他们就努力在任何可能的情况下实施黄金法则。

options.text: It is mainly based on a society's religion.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The golden rule is a moral principle which states that you should treat others the way you want to be treated yourself.信号：开篇“X is...”下定义句即落点 。录音第一句就用 The golden rule is a moral principle which states that you should treat others t…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音确实提到 the religion in their society，但只是说不同人接触到的“形式”受宗教等因素影响，从没说它“mainly based on religion”。A 项盗了 religion 这个原词，把“影响形式的因素之一”偷换成“主要建立在宗教上”，是听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：Different people tend to be exposed to different forms of the golden rule
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：录音说 Different people tend to be exposed to different forms——是“不同人接触不同形式”，B 项 17B 式地改成“interpreted differently in different times”（不同时代有不同解读），把“不同人/不同形式”偷换为“不同时代”，且录音第 3 段强调 all forms... revolve around the same concept（内核其实相同），与 B 相悖。 借用原文：when it conflicts with laws and ethical principles
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：a code of conduct based on laws and ethics 里的 laws and ethics 录音里确实反复出现（如 laws and ethical principles），但那是讲它与法律伦理的“冲突”关系，并非说 golden rule 本身“基于法律伦理”。录音定义它是 a moral principle（道德准则），C 把它的本质错挂到法律伦理上，是张冠李戴式的原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a moral principle which states that you should treat others the way you want to be treated ↔ a moral principle to guide people's behavior “主张你该怎样待人”=“指导人的行为”）

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：A notable criticism of the golden rule is that its application can lead to undesirable outcomes, when it conflicts with laws and ethical principles.信号：信号词 criticism 直接领出答案句 。录音第 4 段以 A notable criticism of the golden rule is that... 开头，criticism 这个批评信号词一出，紧跟的…

transcript.text: Why useless? A team of researchers from the University of Basel published their new study about people's attitudes towards diversity at work. transcript.text: The actual value they attribute to diversity depends on the decision-making perspective. In other words, when a person's own work group is involved, they tend to prefer team members who are similar to themselves. Companies need to pay attention to who makes hiring and team decisions.

transcript.text: Communication can essentially be divided into two categories: the written and the spoken.
transcript.zh: 沟通本质上可以分为两类：书面沟通和口头沟通。

transcript.text: How the balance is struck between these two forms of communication—the point at which one needs to be exchanged for another—really depends on individual cultures.
transcript.zh: 如何在这两种沟通形式之间取得平衡——即在何时需要将一种形式转换为另一种形式——实际上取决于各个文化。

transcript.text: Understanding when it's appropriate to exchange one form for another can be a major key to success in international business.
transcript.zh: 理解何时适合将一种形式转换为另一种形式，可能是国际商务成功的关键因素。

transcript.text: Many cultures place a much greater value on the spoken word than the American working culture does.
transcript.zh: 许多文化对口头语言的重视程度远高于美国职场文化。

transcript.text: In parts of the Middle East, you'll find spoken word agreements are seen as seriously binding. A person's word is linked to their honor, so verbal agreements are seen as important, whereas written contracts are taken as memos of understanding.
transcript.zh: 在中东部分地区,你会发现口头协议被视为具有严肃的约束力。一个人的话语与其荣誉相关联，因此口头协议被视为重要的，而书面合同则被视为理解备忘录。

transcript.text: Western working culture tends to place a high value on the written word, and this reaches its highest level of intensity when it comes to contracts. In the US, France and Germany, written contracts tend to be seen as something that must be strictly carried out.
transcript.zh: 西方职场文化倾向于高度重视书面文字，而这在涉及合同时达到最高强度。在美国、法国和德国，书面合同往往被视为必须严格执行的东西。

transcript.text: By contrast, other cultures may not see written contracts as quite so binding. It can prove a challenge to Western businesses if your business partner wants to renegotiate terms that you thought were already agreed on.
transcript.zh: 相比之下，其他文化可能不认为书面合同具有如此强的约束力。如果你的商业伙伴想要重新协商你认为已经达成一致的条款，这可能会给西方企业带来挑战。

transcript.text: For example, a Japanese firm may have signed a contract, but they may not feel bound by every detail of it—particularly if circumstances later change.
transcript.zh: 例如，一家日本公司可能已经签署了合同，但他们可能不觉得受其每个细节的约束——特别是如果情况后来发生变化。

transcript.text: Such differences in value that different working cultures place on the written word tend to cause many problems when it comes to business relationships.
transcript.zh: 不同职场文化对书面文字所赋予的价值差异，往往会在商业关系中造成许多问题。

If you've ever looked at the ingredients list while grocery shopping, chances are you've seen the term "natural flavors". But have you taken a 26______ to consider what these natural flavors actually are?

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: During the British winter, the thought of two weeks in a coastal villa(别墅) with soul-stirring views of the sea and a huge pool to enjoy is enough to offset(抵消) the labor until the holidays start. For a growing number of people, however, their yearly break is turning into a nightmare as they find that the property they have paid thousands for does not exist and the website through which they booked it has disappeared.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Consumers have been warned to be aware of the potential for deception in this market, which is far from uncommon. In 2017 there were 1,632 cases of reported "villa fraud(诈骗)", with victims losing an average of £2,052, according to Action Fraud, the national center for reporting such frauds. "Millions of pounds are lost each year by defrauded holidaymakers," says Sean Tipton of the Association of British Travel Agents (ABTA).

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The problem has ballooned in the last 10 years, with frauds becoming more and more sophisticated. The fake websites have authentic-sounding names involving a mix of keywords, typically including the place name, "summer", "villas" or "rentals". Details of legitimate(合法的) villas are often stolen from other sites. "When the fraudsters first started it was unsophisticated—the websites looked amateur and there wasn't a lot of effort," says Tipton. "Now they are clever. They extensively rip off legitimate websites and use a different website name. They'll have pictures of a sales team and it might be a poor actor in New York that is down as their head of sales."

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Fraudsters target popular seaside destinations for British tourists visiting Spain where prices can soar if demand exceeds supply. Prices are kept within reasonable ranges to avoid arousing suspicion. "A villa might cost £5,000 elsewhere and they will offer it at say £3,500. But a bit of a giveaway is that the villa will be cheaper than on other websites and there's unlimited availability," says Tipton. Fraudsters also invest in pay-per-click advertising to feature at the top of search engines when people type in phrases such as "Spanish seaside villas".

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: With such a degree of professionalism, how can consumers find out if the website they're looking to book with is trustworthy? "When people book holiday villas they are doing so through rose-colored glasses," says Tony Neate, chief executive of Get Safe Online, "They should be Googling the property, and looking on websites like Google Maps and StreetView to see if it's there. Also, speak to the person you're booking the villa with on a landline phone, as fraudsters tend to only use mobiles." He also suggests asking someone not going on the holiday to have a look at the website. "They might spot problems you don't spot." Another potential red flag is being asked to pay by bank transfer. "The problem is that when the money leaves your account it's in theirs straightaway and it's very hard to track it," says Barclays Bank head of digital safety, Jodie Gilbert. "We generally recommend other forms of payment, like credit card."

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Little seems to be known about these fraudsters, "There is no way to definitely know who they are," says Neate. "It could be anyone. It could be your next-door neighbor or organized crime in Russia." Action Fraud says people should ensure the company renting the villa is a member of a recognized trade body such as ABTA.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: "By working with industry partners such as ABTA and Get Safe Online, we are able to issue alerts about the latest threats they should be aware of. If you believe you have fallen victim to fraud or cyber-crime, please report it to Action Fraud," it adds. ABTA says it is trying to combat the issue by running public awareness campaigns. "It's a growing problem and people can't stop fraudsters being dishonest," says Tipton. "They're still going to do it. It's not impossible to stop but as it's internet-based it's harder to pursue."

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Nick Cooper, the founder and co-owner of villa booking company Villa Plus, estimates his company has uncovered more than 200 fake villa websites over the past two years, and doesn't believe enough is being done. "It is hopeless to report fake villa websites to the internet giants who host them," he says. "I found it impossible to speak to anyone. Also, once one bank account gets reported, they simply use another."

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: For now the only way to stop fraudsters appears ultimately to lie in the hands of the consumer. "When people book their holidays they get so emotionally involved, and when they find that villa at a good price with availability in peak season, they are an easy target," says Cooper. "The public has to learn to be far more aware they are a target for these sort of frauds." But it's not just the financial cost. "A family will turn up at a villa and find out it doesn't exist or the owner doesn't know who you are," says Tipton. "The problem then is you have to find accommodation at short notice. It can be incredibly expensive but it's the emotional cost, too."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Carla O'Shaughnessy from Sydenham was searching last year for a good deal to book a villa in Majorca for a summer break for the family. "I was comparing prices online and found one that came in a bit cheaper than others," says O'Shaughnessy. She emailed the company via its website, asking how far the villa was from the airport and about local restaurants. "They came back with believable answers; it was all very friendly and professional," she says. Happy with the responses, O'Shaughnessy paid the full amount of £ 3,000 via bank transfer into the travel agent's account and then forgot about it until a month before the booking.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: "I tried logging on to the website and couldn't," she recalls. "I Googled the agent's name and there were lots of complaints about him being a fraudster. If only I'd Googled before but I never thought of it." Although she found another villa in time for their holiday, she admits she was much more cautious. "I paid through a secure third-party site and had phone conversations with the agent. But I wasn't able to relax until we turned up and I had the keys."

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: In the coming era of budget cuts to education, distance learning could become the norm.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The temptation for those in charge of education budgets to trade teachers for technology could be so strong that they ignore the disadvantages of distance learning. School facilities are expensive to build and maintain, and teachers are expensive to employ. Online classes do not require buildings and each class can host hundreds of people simultaneously, resulting in greater savings, thus increasing the temptation of distance education for those concerned more about budgets than learning. But moving away from a traditional classroom in which a living, breathing human being teaches and interacts with students daily would be a disaster. Physically attending school has hidden benefits: getting up every morning, interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers are essential skills to cultivate in young people. Moreover, schools should be more than simple institutions of traditional learning. They are now places that provide meals. They are places where students receive counseling and other support.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Those policy-makers are often fascinated by the latest technology in education and its potential to "transform" education overnight. But online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help. Educational videos may deliver academic content, but they are unable to make eye contact or assess a student's level of engagement. Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom. In their first 18 years of life, American children spend only 9% of their time in school. Yet teachers are expected to prepare them to be responsible citizens, cultivate their social skills, encourage successful time management, and enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market. Given these expectations, schools should not become permanently "remote".

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time. Personal teaching is about teachers showing students a higher path, and about young people going through the process together. Technology, no matter how advanced, should simply be a tool of a good teacher.

【参考译文】
Long long ago, there was a man who raised a flock of sheep. One morning, when he was about to take the sheep out to graze, he found that one of them was missing. On a closer look, he saw that there was a hole in the sheepfold. Obviously, during the night a wolf had got into the sheepfold and carried off a sheep. His neighbour advised him to mend the sheepfold, but he would not listen. The next day, he found that another sheep had been carried off by the wolf through the hole. Remembering what his neighbour had said, he quickly blocked up the hole and mended the sheepfold. From then on, his sheep were never carried off by wolves again. The story tells us that fixing problems in time can prevent us from suffering greater losses.
